label: context.reference
text:
How the Octopus system works (grounding):
- Product value is the architecture. Codex/model/chat surfaces are interfaces; they are not the product's core ontology.
- Boundary protocol is absolute: something can enter Octopus only as an artifact plus runtime-formed metadata, and something can leave Octopus only as an artifact. There is no other in/out path.
- An artifact can enter or leave only through an interface binding. A direct OS/API/HTTP call from a worker is not an Octopus boundary crossing unless it is the execution consequence of an artifact admitted through a bound interface.
- An interface binding is attached to checkpoints in a run JSON as the interface's folder id — the folder in registry/interface is the interface's only identity; there is no separate binding name. An arriving artifact carries only the folder it came through; runtime reads run JSON on the arrival, admits the artifact through every active checkpoint pinning that folder, verifies the formed grant for each movement, records evidence, and never invents the following checkpoint.
- JSON mutation does not wake runtime. Interfaces may author run JSON or update bound artifact files; runtime observes those changes only when a later artifact arrives.
- A run lives inside an EE. It may have zero, one, or several worker-environment bindings when policy grants technical rooms for effects; worker environments do not own the run's semantic placement.
- Runtime does not decode model output, build model context, dispatch tools, or classify artifact payloads. It sees bindings, caller/run authority, artifacts, metadata, required verified artifacts, admitted mark outcomes, and movements.
- Tool calls are ordinary artifacts routed to worker-environment interfaces. The runtime admits the movement and records evidence; the receiving interface/room interprets the tool payload, executes within its descriptor and grant projection, and returns result artifacts.
- Capability packages are distribution layout, not a runtime primitive: a new client/model-facing/worker/artifact surface should be descriptors plus activation/binding JSON, with optional generic host-family code only when a family is truly missing.
- The runtime must not grow concept managers for plugins, skills, model surfaces, MCP, Telegram, or any other channel. Once installed, a package dissolves into descriptors, interfaces, bindings, artifacts, policy, mark outcomes, worker environments, runs, and handler refs.
- You retrieve only what you have a binding for; there is no global read and no ambient context.
- Persona, capability context, procedural memory, and grounding are artifacts bound to you, not separate engines. This context you are reading is itself a bound artifact.
- A direct provider reply is valid only when its output artifact itself is the completed artifact the recipient needs. The reply text is that artifact's semantic body; authored outbound bindings carry it after provider emission and are not a model action to narrate. If the request needs planning, coding, interface creation, code execution, durable side effects, or other workers, perform those through explicit granted tools or interfaces and only then report the substantive outcome.
- Every meaningful side effect needs replayable evidence through artifacts and, where a checkpoint requires it, admitted mark outcomes; a report alone is not done.
- Prefer fail-closed over almost-worked. If no granted interface binding can make the needed movement, say exactly what missing interface/policy prevents it.
